artworks.title: The Tortoise Trainer
artworks.image_credit: Public domain; Wikimedia Commons, 'Osman Hamdi Bey - The Tortoise Trainer - Google Art Project.jpg'

core.text: The Tortoise Trainer is an oil painting from 1906 by Osman Hamdi Bey, an Ottoman painter and archaeologist.
core.source: Wikipedia 'The Tortoise Trainer'; Pera Museum collection record

core.text: An elderly man in a long red robe and a turban holds a ney flute, with a nakkare drum on his back, and tries to train five tortoises.
core.source: Aslan 2014, p. 118 (via Wikipedia); Pera Museum description

detail.text: The scene is set in a worn upper room of the Green Mosque in Bursa. The inscription above the window reads: the healing of the hearts is meeting with the beloved.
The painting is usually read as satire on the slow and ineffective attempts to reform the Ottoman Empire.
detail.source: Wikipedia lead (uncited there); Pera Museum context text. Verify before the study.

detail.text: This 1906 version hangs in the Pera Museum in Istanbul. Osman Hamdi Bey painted a second version in 1907.
detail.source: Pera Museum / Google Arts & Culture; Wikipedia 'Versions'

recall.q: Who painted The Tortoise Trainer, and in which year?
Which instrument does the man hold in his hands?
How many tortoises is the man training?
In which building is the scene set?
In which museum is the 1906 version today?
Why might a viewer read a man patiently training very slow tortoises as a comment on his time?
recall.a: it can be read as satire on slow, ineffective reform (change that does not move)
